title: 12 Nov Microsoft 365 outage: preliminary PIR blames July gateway bug
summary: Microsoft's preliminary post-incident report (in the Microsoft 365 admin center) ties the roughly 24-hour outage on 12–13 November, worst for Exchange Online, to a latent bug in a July update to its networking gateway servers, triggered by extra traffic after Teams failed over onto the same infrastructure while about 14% of gateway capacity was already offline. At the worst point more than 80% of gateway servers were unresponsive; Teams, OneDrive and SharePoint failed over and recovered earlier, Exchange Online could not. Microsoft says a final report is due later this week.
why: Your SLA claims, internal incident reviews and any 'mail continuity' business cases need Microsoft's own wording, not press summaries. The PIR also shows that region isolation did not contain the failure, which matters for resilience assumptions.
todo: Download the preliminary PIR from Service health > History in the admin center now, and the final PIR when it is published.
Check whether the downtime breaches the Online Services SLA for your licences and file any service-credit claim within the contractual window.
Add 'Exchange Online unavailable globally for 24 h' to your BCP scenarios (alternative comms, journaling/continuity).
